speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the specific movements you are experiencing and when they first began?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned a new movement disorder; can you describe the specific abnormal movements you are experiencing, such as tremors, rigidity, or involuntary facial grimacing? Also, have you noticed any signs of restlessness or an inability to sit still since starting the risperidone?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your symptoms of inner restlessness and the need to keep moving are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. I will reduce your risperidone dose and start a beta-blocker like propranolol to help manage these symptoms. DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia
